newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. adds 262,000 new jobs in Dec.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. adds 262,000 new jobs in Dec.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the U.S. economy created 262,000 new jobs in December after a revised 127,000 gain in November.
The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.3 percent.
Experts in a Reuters survey had expected 192,000 new jobs to have been created in the month and a jobless rate of 5.3.
MICHAEL ENGLUND, CHIEF ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL INC:
"This report is certainly great for the economy, it's going to be a disaster for bonds."
Englund was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.
WARD MCCARTHY, MANAGING DIRECTOR, STONE & MCCARTHY

RESEARCH ASSOCIATES INC: "It's just plain strong and it's bad news for bonds. There was a real sharp rise in earnings, the market won't like it and it's going to make the Fed nervous. It's just going to resurrect concerns that labor market conditions are too tight."
On whether the report could move up expectations for a Fed tightening: "Oh sure, this will definitely cause some concerns on that front."
RICHARD BERNER, EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT AND CHIEF

ECONOMIST, MELLON BANK CORP: "The numbers are strong across the board in terms of growth. Moreover, we've got a big increase in average hourly earnings following what we had last month, five-tenths after eight-tenths percent.

"We got the unemployment rate at 5.3 perecent and as you know we had revised data across the board in this report as they always do. We see that November's unemployment rate was revised somewhat lower and so were the prior months.

"So, on balance, the unemployment rate hasn't dropped further, but what we're looking at is strong jobs growth, a "So, on balance, the unemployment rate hasn't dropped further, but what we're looking at is strong jobs growth, a low unemployment rate and upward pressure on wages."
DONALD MAUDE, CHIEF U.S. ECONOMIST, SCOTIA CAPITAL MARKETS
INC: "There's nothing weak in this number. There's nothing in terms of downward revisions to offset this.
"Underneath the surface, it's very strong. Average hourly earnings up five-tenths (of a percent), year-over-year (it's) now 3.8 percent.

"You're going to get a very strong industrial production, probably around 0.7, maybe 0.6 percent higher. You're going to get a very strong personal income number out of this, probably 0.6 (percent). You're probably going to see upward revisions to (Gross Domestic Product), probably 3.5 to 4.0 percent. "Even though I don't think they'll move in February, I think you're going to have speculation about a February tightening."
DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO

INTERNATIONAL INC: "You're looking at a strong performance this month ... You got a very large increase in manufacturing output, that man-hours index with employee hours index up 0.8, and you look at the weekly hours -- that's really impressive. "You can take special factors, you can point fingers here and there, but ... you are still looking at a strong (economic) picture."
-- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660
